newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea adds conditions to oil price deregulation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea adds conditions to oil price deregulation.

text.p: South Korea added new conditions to oil price deregulation by asking oil refiners to report to the government before they change prices of gasoline, kerosene and diesel for the first six months after oil prices are deregulated next year, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said on Tuesday.
The ministry said in a statement that after the six-month period, refiners would only have to report changes after the fact.
"This measure should minimise any side-effects from the price deregulation and help the government to foresee price movement," the statement said.
The ministry said it would also take "a minimum level of administrative measures" against refiners if there is too much volatility in prices hurting the stability of the economy.
No details were provided on the possible steps.
The ministry also said it would attempt to prevent any price fixing among refiners or other violations of law.

Under the present system, the sales price for each of these products has a fixed ceiling. On the first day of each month, refiners, sales agents and service stations are informed of the prices by the ministry and the Korea Petroleum Association.
Prices fluctuate according to the previous month's crude oil prices and product prices in the Singapore spot market.
